outcome: distribution of public health financing benefits/subsidies
cohort: The study included 3360 women (age 15-49 years) from Bangladesh who had an institutional delivery during the two years preceding the 2022 survey.
finding: Public health subsidies in Bangladesh equitably benefit women with lower income, though inequities remain in tertiary care facilities and for caesarean deliveries, and women with lower income are more vulnerable to distress financing for delivery care.
mod_finding: For caesarean delivery, the wealthiest group benefitted the most from public subsidies, receiving 26% of them.
cross-section timing: Data was collected through the Bangladesh Demographic and Health Survey (BDHS) 2022, covering institutional deliveries that occurred within two years prior to the survey.
